source.title: Armagh Guardian, 3 June 1927, p. 3 (list of the new county council: "Returned Unopposed" and "Retiring Councillors deemed to be re-elected"); nominations from the Newry Reporter, 28 April 1927, p. 6 ("County Elections: Nominations in Armagh")
source.publisher: Armagh Guardian (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every name checked against the two page images; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Triennial election of the county council, 1927: nominations received by Thomas E. Reid, secretary, 26 April 1927; the only poll was in Portadown, 26 May 1927. No party labels are printed for the unopposed members in the nominations or the list of the new council, so none are given. Returned unopposed. The nomination lists in the Newry Reporter and the Portadown News print the second name as "H. C. Nicholson"; the list of the new council gives Malcolm. John S. Carrick: no party label printed in 1927. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Lurgan, Lurgan Urban District, 15 January 1923, listed as Unionist: Lurgan Mail, 6 January 1923, p. 5 (advertisement "Lurgan Municipal Election, January 1923": the fifteen candidates adopted by the Joint Committee of the Orange Institution and other local Unionist organisations); Lurgan Mail, 13 January 1923, p. 5 ("Notes and Notions": "the unchallenged return of fifteen Unionist candidates"); Lurgan, Lurgan Urban District, 15 January 1927, listed as Unionist: Belfast News-Letter, 7 January 1927, p. 8 (provincial nominations); Lurgan, Lurgan Urban District, 15 January 1930, listed as Unionist: Lurgan Mail, 18 January 1930, p. 3 ("The Municipal Election"); labels from the Portadown Times, 10 January 1930, p. 1 ("Lurgan Urban Elections")). Herbert C. Malcolm: no party label printed in 1927. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Lurgan, Lurgan Urban District, 15 January 1923, listed as Unionist: Lurgan Mail, 6 January 1923, p. 5 (advertisement "Lurgan Municipal Election, January 1923": the fifteen candidates adopted by the Joint Committee of the Orange Institution and other local Unionist organisations); Lurgan Mail, 13 January 1923, p. 5 ("Notes and Notions": "the unchallenged return of fifteen Unionist candidates"); Lurgan, Lurgan Urban District, 15 January 1926, listed as Unionist: Frontier Sentinel, 9 January 1926, p. 5 ("No Lurgan Opposition"); Lurgan, Lurgan Urban District, 15 January 1929, listed as Unionist: Lurgan Mail, 12 January 1929, p. 2 ("Lurgan Municipal Election: No Contest")).
